mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment falls below 3.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production and housing starts both increase, it indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both indicators increase but S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns do not decrease in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS grows but S&P 500 returns do not increase in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates lower inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If CPI decreases but S&P 500 returns are not positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) increase, it signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both indicators increase but S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated.
